target_customer: Companies deploying AI agents that call third-party APIs and tools, including agencies running agents for multiple clients, and software firms whose agents act inside customer accounts
problem: AI agents often hold long-lived credentials and broad permissions, so a mistaken or hijacked tool call can touch production systems. Alter wraps each call in authentication, policy checks and audit.
business_model: Freemium developer platform: free plan with 10,000 API calls per month, paid tiers via demo (not listed)
product_category: Identity and access control for AI agents (auth proxy, privileged access management)

founders.name: Srikar Dandamuraju
founders.background_notes: Education not listed on the YC page.

founders.name: Kevan Dodhia
previous_startups: Compute.ai (technical co-founder, acquired by Terizza in 2025)
founders.background_notes: Education not stated in the sources opened.

technical_complexity.rationale: A credential-injecting auth proxy with policy engine, 150+ provider integrations and audit logging is standard security infrastructure with some hard parts such as parameter-level authorization and credential rotation. A two person team with distributed systems experience could build it.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and policy configuration create some lock-in once adopted, but the concept is easy to copy and larger identity vendors and well funded startups target the same wedge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Within months of the S25 batch, agent identity startups such as Keycard (October 2025, 38 million dollars) and Scalekit (September 2025) announced funding. Later entrants, not competition at founding.

market_need_then: In 2025 agent adoption raised concern over agents holding long-lived secrets and acting with excess permissions. Press at the time described non-human identities outnumbering human ones in enterprises.

branding.domain_note: Uses alterauth.com; a directory says an earlier alter.ai domain is no longer used by the company (unverified).

identity.voice_and_tone: Direct, technical and confident, with imperative headlines and phrases like deny by default and fail closed

branding.community_and_virality: Presented on Hacker News as a privileged access management layer for agents; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Clear security voice, but the name Alter is generic and shared with other companies (a 2021 seed round belongs to a different Alter), and no brand press or community was found.

outcome_analysis: Alter is an active two person company from the Summer 2025 batch selling agent access control as the market for agent security formed. A prior exit by the CTO and infrastructure experience of the CEO fit the problem. Funding beyond a DeVC investment is not confirmed, and well funded agent identity entrants appeared within months, so the outcome is still open.
notes: A 500K pre-seed figure appears only on VC Backed, an aggregator with a wrong location for the company, so it is unverified and not recorded as a round. Competition list is empty because no source dated near the June 2025 batch was found; the agent identity startups found were dated after the batch. No outcome news found for Alter itself. A 2021 seed round for another company named Alter was ignored.
